title: Key Schedules Avoiding Weak Expanded Keys
summary: Expanded-key analysis exposes potentially weak keys, but constructing a concrete schedule that excludes all resulting weak sets remains open.

formal_statement.body: Construct a key schedule whose reachable expanded keys avoid every identified weak expanded-key set.

scope.domain: Block-cipher key-schedule design informed by fixed-key differential analysis.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a key schedule whose reachable expanded keys avoid every identified weak expanded-key set.

citations.label: Understanding Unexpected Fixed-Key Differential Behaviours: How to Avoid Major Weaknesses in Lightweight Designs

progress.summary: The source presents a two-step design approach: identify potential weaknesses in the expanded-key model, then develop a key schedule that mitigates them. It advocates the absence of weak expanded keys as a design principle.
citation_labels: Anne Canteaut et al., Understanding Unexpected Fixed-Key Differential Behaviours: How to Avoid Major Weaknesses in Lightweight Designs
